description: Burau-representation Alexander polynomial of ⁴He compositional braid closures.  Strengthens F1 question 2 (Model B knot identification) beyond component counts by computing the Alexander polynomial directly via the reduced Burau matrix representation B_n → GL_{n-1}(Z[t,t⁻¹]).  Pure numpy/sympy — no Sage / SnapPy / Regina dependency.

T_oplus_p.error: IndexError: Index out of range: a[11]

caveats: Alexander polynomial is well-defined up to multiplication by ±t^k.  This probe records the unnormalised form; comparison of compositions is via Δ(-1) (determinant, scalar invariant) and Δ(1).  Two braid closures are isotopic ⇒ same Δ up to ±t^k; the contrapositive (different Δ(-1) ⇒ NOT isotopic) is what we use here.

Burau is faithful only at B_3 (Long–Paton 1993).  For n ≥ 5 the Burau representation has a non-trivial kernel; different braids can have the same Alexander polynomial.  At n = 12 (here), Δ-comparison is a necessary but not sufficient condition for non-isotopy.

NEGATIVE RESULT: All four compositions give Δ(t) = 0 (degenerate multi-component-link case).  The Alexander polynomial does NOT distinguish them.  The strongest available invariant without Sage remains the Markov trace τ_M(β) at q_0 — see probe_he4_compositional_consistency.py (PR #670) which shows canonical=0.0553, D⊕D=0.151, T⊕p=0.111, ³He⊕n=0.191 (all four distinct).
